common_mistakes: Assuming outlet replacement is always exempt — adding GFCI protection can still require an electrical permit in St. Louis.
Using the wrong permit category or trying to file under a building permit instead of electrical.
Installing GFCI devices without verifying line/load wiring, which causes nuisance trips and failed inspection.
Submitting the application with the wrong jurisdiction — St. Louis city is not St. Louis County.

pro_tips: Because St. Louis City uses a flat residential electrical fee, the permit cost should stay at $85 even if the job value is only $1,200.
Label the existing circuit before swapping devices so you can keep line/load straight on each GFCI and avoid callbacks.
Take a photo of each existing box before replacement in case the inspector asks whether the boxes were already in place and undisturbed.
